designStatus: Original source-fit framework assessment designs; not actual learner observations, validated scales or universally selected language materials.

requiredBeforeUse: Actual language in role R1 or R2, with distinct role evidence.
Familiarity and applicability of the precise unfamiliar-R2 source exception.
Authorised, locally suitable materials and accepted response/scoring specification checked by a competent speaker/script user.
Prompting, access and assistance recorded separately from independent performance.
notInferred: English or R1 mastery transferring automatically to any other language.
An age-three deadline for a stage-end operation.
A learner-state score, attitude label or compatibility authorisation.

protocols.task: Maintain two separate role-labelled portfolios, with the oral tasks below carried out using a locally appropriate language in each role. Integrate them in a small shared activity without turning the stage goals into isolated textbook units.
evidenceDesign: Record language role, actual language, familiarity, prompt language, assessor competence and assistance for every task.
Use the unfamiliar-R2 exception only where its source condition actually applies: emergence at Foundational stage end and consolidation early in Preparatory.
A conversation, instruction exchange, literary response, original verse, narrative and vocabulary-inference case are separately designed in each role.
nearMisses: One English portfolio copied into both roles.
Expecting the same fluency at age three as at stage end.
Treating a source goal association as a learner mastery certificate.
protocols.transfer: Change partner and familiar everyday setting in each role.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: All component protocols apply; success in one role is not evidence of the other, and unqualified graph links are withheld where inherited English gates prevent faithful representation.

protocols.task: A competent speaker introduces a short local song, chant and poem, with culturally suitable rhythm and intelligible oral delivery. Invite joining a repeated pattern, noticing a sound or image, and explaining a chosen phrase.
evidenceDesign: Replicate a beat and a repeated sound pattern; distinguish this from merely copying an action.
Discuss a recurring phrase, an image or sensory word and its effect in the actual language.
Offer a different favourite or a reason for not choosing a text without penalty.
nearMisses: Accurate clapping offered as the sole evidence of meaning.
Requiring enthusiastic enjoyment or a prescribed favourite.
protocols.transfer: Use a new orally introduced poem with a different repeating pattern.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Rhythm claim includes clapping/tapping and timed joining; expressive-language claim includes recurring story language as well as poetic sensory wording. A short story supplies that additional whole-claim case.

protocols.task: Invite an original short verse about a familiar event without supplying its full lines. The child chooses a repeated phrase, a sound pattern or a rhyme, then reshapes it into a short singable verse using a familiar melody.
evidenceDesign: Keep an authorship record distinguishing child-created wording from adult prompts.
Create a new line or meaningful variation rather than only reciting a memorised model.
An adult may record or transcribe the oral contribution; R2 written production is not smuggled into this oral standard.
nearMisses: Only repeating the adult-written verse.
Changing one supplied name without control of the pattern.
protocols.transfer: Create a new verse for a different familiar situation.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Writing Poetry contributes composition. Its complete written, rhyme/rhythm and memorised expressive-recitation operation can be assessed through R1 writing and a suitable rhyme task at stage end; oral R2 evidence alone does not certify the whole written topic. The source task need not impose rhyme on every poem.

protocols.task: Use an everyday collaborative choice or shared planning exchange, then ask for a short description of a familiar event. The adult does not script each response.
evidenceDesign: Maintain several relevant turns, respond to what the partner actually says, and repair a misunderstanding.
Give enough ordered detail for the listener to follow; evaluate intelligibility in the actual language, not English accent.
Respect appropriate local interaction conventions and accessibility; eye contact is not a universal compulsory display.

Use stage-appropriate connected, responsive talk in familiar situations. Distinguish sustained word-search that repeatedly prevents meaning, or wholly rehearsed turns that cannot adapt to a response, from an intelligible connected exchange. Do not impose native-speaker speed or an accent target. The very-unfamiliar-R2 emergence exception remains applicable; this is not an identical fluency deadline for both roles.
nearMisses: A memorised monologue with no response to a partner.
Adult translates every utterance while the result is labelled independent role fluency.
protocols.transfer: Change partner and topic while retaining a familiar, low-stakes setting.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Complete discussion operation includes listening, turn exchange and sustained topic focus; the description operation adds clear, logically organised details.

protocols.task: Use a safe four-step physical task. One partner hears and follows instructions, asks for clarification when a deliberately ambiguous step appears, then gives a fresh ordered sequence and repairs a partner misunderstanding.
evidenceDesign: Retain all four steps and their order.
Clarification changes an actual ambiguity rather than parroting a model question.
The result lets the speaker locate and repair the unclear instruction.
nearMisses: Only following one command.
Receiving instructions accurately but never giving any.
protocols.transfer: Give instructions for a different material task to a new partner.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete intrinsic instruction operation and both unchanged hard prerequisites are accounted by role-appropriate tasks. The registered question-word correction removes the excessive full-inventory hard gate; no English question-word inventory is imposed on arbitrary R1/R2.

protocols.task: Read or narrate an unfamiliar short story beyond independent reading level, and a short factual text. Ask for characters, event sequence, connected details and a defensible message using source evidence.
evidenceDesign: Separate answering about an adult-read text from independent decoding.
Ask for a message supported by events rather than a forced moral for every story.
Invite a clarification question and an explanation of how two factual details relate.
nearMisses: Only naming pictured characters.
Repeating an adult-supplied moral without supporting events.
protocols.transfer: Use a second narrative with a different event order and a different informational topic.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Listening includes poems, stories and non-fiction; story-structure and central-message claims include sequence and informational connections, not only plot naming.

protocols.task: After a familiar short story, invite an oral telling with identifiable people and ordered events, followed by a child-chosen alternative ending that remains understandable.
evidenceDesign: Retain the telling’s beginning, event relation and ending.
Listen for descriptive details and clear organisation, without requiring English connectives.
Differentiate retelling from independent original authorship; this task does not alone certify written narrative composition.
nearMisses: Repeating disconnected character names.
Adult supplies the event sequence one line at a time.
protocols.transfer: Tell a different short story or familiar personal event to a listener who did not hear the original.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete story-element operation includes key tales, setting and sequential retelling; the description operation includes people, places, things and events.

protocols.task: Use brief role-appropriate oral/text contexts containing familiar words and one unfamiliar word whose meaning can be inferred. Ask for a tentative meaning, its contextual support and a useful application in another exchange.
evidenceDesign: Connect an unfamiliar word to known vocabulary and context/pictures; allow correction after new evidence.
Use a newly encountered word appropriately in conversation and, for whole-topic writing evidence, an R1 written context.
Include everyday interactions beyond a single rehearsed text.

Test functional adequacy across varied relevant exchanges: express a need or choice, seek help, and respond or clarify. Defining or inserting one new word is insufficient by itself. Judge whether useful meaning is communicated in context, with role-appropriate support recorded; no universal vocabulary count is invented.
nearMisses: Adult gives the definition before the inference is recorded.
Repeating a new word with incompatible meaning.
protocols.transfer: Introduce a different unknown word with new contextual clues, then change the everyday situation.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The root-free existing vocabulary candidate already includes inference from context and pictures. No Greek/Latin-root prerequisite or universal word list is added. A known English word does not establish the corresponding word in R1 or R2.

protocols.task: A competent speaker selects familiar words with clearly analysable spoken syllables in the task language. Use counters or claps to count and separate syllables, then join orally supplied syllable sequences. Alongside a familiar written word, mark its spoken pronunciation divisions as an aid, without equating syllable divisions with letter or akshar boundaries.
evidenceDesign: Count, blend and segment several novel-to-task words rather than memorising one sequence.
Join supplied units without an answer picture giving away the word.
Expert-check syllable boundaries in the actual language and distinguish oral divisions from script units.
nearMisses: Counting visible letters instead of spoken units.
Imposing English syllable boundaries or silently testing a fixed English phoneme inventory.
protocols.transfer: Use familiar words with different syllable lengths in the same role, then repeat the design independently in the other role.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The whole Syllables claim includes spoken counting/blending/segmentation plus written-word pronunciation support. The source permits this syllable route; it does not oblige an English consonant-cluster task. Script-symbol recognition is separately conditioned.

protocols.task: Use a real or authorised facsimile book and short functional text in the task script. Ask the child to locate the starting point, follow the actual reading path, show page progression, distinguish printed words from illustration and explain a familiar punctuation cue.
evidenceDesign: Bind direction, word-boundary conventions and punctuation to the actual script and edition.
Include a book-layout case, a word-in-print case and a punctuation-in-context case.
A qualified speaker/script user checks every model and response criterion.
nearMisses: Accepting left-to-right finger tracking as universal.
Calling an akshar a Latin letter or using an unsupported punctuation inventory.
protocols.transfer: Use a second layout in the same script while preserving its conventions.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: No unconditional Understanding print or English sentence-punctuation link is published. This retains a formal source requirement, with an explicit script-binding representation condition.

protocols.task: Record the actual role language, script, locally applicable authoritative symbol inventory and taught/frequent subset. For R1, test the complete source-required inventory; for emergent R2, test its source-required frequent subset, then meaningful reading and productive use in words and simple sentences.
evidenceDesign: Provide mixed-order recognition and meaningful word use, not alphabet recitation alone.
Record which forms belong to the inventory and which occur frequently in the selected R2 materials.
Differentiate symbol knowledge, decoding and productive text; no fixed English letter count is assumed.
nearMisses: Treating all 26 English letters as the inventory for every script.
Assuming R1 symbols have identical sound/function in R2.
Inventing a universal frequent-symbol count.
protocols.transfer: Use previously unpractised words or a new simple sentence within the declared material inventory.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Current English all-letter and single-letter-sound claims contain specific inventory requirements. Candidate mappings remain conditional and no universal unqualified link is authored.

protocols.task: Choose a short R1 text whose linguistic units and vocabulary fit the intended stage-end task. Use a first read, reread and a second passage; record accuracy, phrasing, expressive pauses and self-correction in the actual language.
evidenceDesign: Specify local scoring units and an expert-checked accepted reading before use.
Keep the existing basic-reading accuracy check and rereading component when assessing that whole claim.
Separate fluent sounding from comprehension through an independent meaning question.
nearMisses: Using English GPC or left-to-right knowledge as a prerequisite in a different script.
Declaring fluency after an adult rehearses every line.
protocols.transfer: Read a new passage with a different mood and familiar vocabulary.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The intrinsic expressive-reading operation is shared. Its hard chain to basic reading, then fixed English phonemes and left-to-right print, is not universally appropriate; the graph association is withheld pending a separate reviewed dependency decision.

protocols.task: Supply a short R1 story for independent reading, then ask for its people, event sequence, important details and an evidenced central meaning. Add a brief factual text to check how pieces of information connect.
evidenceDesign: No adult read-aloud substitutes for the independent-reading condition.
Support a message with a meaningful event or detail, allowing different defensible interpretations.
Ask one simple inference from what a character says or does.
nearMisses: Only recalling the book cover or naming its author.
Heard-story performance offered as independent reading.
protocols.transfer: Use a second narrative not rehearsed in the listening task.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Story sequence/message includes informational connections and the inference prerequisite; all are included without importing a fixed English decoding inventory into these intrinsically shared comprehension operations.

protocols.task: Use a short independently readable R1 poem and a short story. Ask about an interesting phrase, a recurring pattern and a sensory image; invite the child to explain why a wording choice works.
evidenceDesign: Interpret wording in its actual context rather than translating an English word-by-word rubric.
Keep recurring literary-language and sensory-expression checks in the whole claim.
Accept a reasoned preference or dislike; the task is interpretation, not forced enjoyment.
nearMisses: Only spotting rhyme endings without interpreting any words.
Requiring the adult’s preferred feeling or favourite line.
protocols.transfer: Use a second poem with different imagery and repetition.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The existing expressive/sensory-language claim and its read-aloud prerequisite are retained; no meter/haiku or English simile-marker bundle is silently imposed.

protocols.task: Use a short child-appropriate news item, an instruction or recipe, and a publicity notice in R1. Ask what each communicates, identify its purpose, and carry out a safe supplied instruction or identify the intended response.
evidenceDesign: Identify main information and supporting details, including a connection between two details.
Distinguish informative, action-guiding, entertaining and persuasive purposes using a small contrasting set.
A recipe task uses supplied measures/materials so advanced measurement is not a hidden literacy prerequisite.
nearMisses: Only identifying a text’s genre without comprehending its message.
Reading a title offered as evidence of following its instructions.
protocols.transfer: Use another brief real-world text with different layout and purpose.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The whole main-topic and text-purpose claims include their genre/author/illustrator prerequisite checks; short suitable story/poem/non-fiction examples supply that broader prerequisite task without a language-specific alphabet requirement.

protocols.task: In R1, author a focused experience paragraph and a short two-part informational piece with meaningful groups and a heading where useful. Explain one boundary, then repair a misplaced fact or boundary in a separate supplied text.
evidenceDesign: Group related ideas around a focus rather than merely write three unrelated sentences.
Retain the complete paragraph claim’s narrative and non-narrative organisational cases.
Use an expert-checked target-language text model without requiring the English names of every writing-process term.
nearMisses: Adult dictates the paragraph boundaries.
Counting lines alone used to identify a paragraph.
protocols.transfer: Reorganise another short text in which the topic changes at a different point.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete paragraph operation retains focused grouping, narrative/non-narrative organisational cases and purposeful headings. The three broader process-vocabulary/narrative/stamina requirements remain useful soft support after separate review; they are not mandatory whole bundles before this operation.

protocols.task: Provide accessible, varied age-appropriate R1 books or equivalent accessible texts, a real opportunity to borrow or revisit them, and repeated low-stakes invitations to choose. Ask what makes a choice appealing, without prescribing the response.
evidenceDesign: Record available choice and access, not a stable learner trait or a compulsory reading quota.
Separate barriers such as inaccessible print, material scarcity and unfamiliar language from unwillingness.
Accept declining a book, changing preferences or needing help.
nearMisses: Treating a lack of eye contact or visible enthusiasm as failure.
Using accurate oral reading or recommending a book as proof of voluntary interest.
protocols.transfer: Offer a different accessible text collection after another interval and preserve the changed context.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: This is a retained contextual engagement requirement. No new binary interest/mastery topic, learner field or score is added.

protocols.task: Combine independent narrative/poetry/functional reading and paragraph writing with an explicitly bound R1 script/print inventory. Use shared materials where appropriate while retaining evidence for each requirement.
evidenceDesign: Distinguish actual-language knowledge from cross-language shared process contributions.
Retain the conditional script requirements rather than treating generic reading links as a complete literacy certificate.
nearMisses: Calling all R1 literacy Full graph coverage from story comprehension alone.
protocols.transfer: Use another short integrated R1 reading/writing task.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: All named component protocols and current graph-compatibility limits remain explicit.

protocols.task: Combine R2 syllable analysis and a declared frequent-symbol/word/sentence task with role-appropriate support. Preserve the difference between emergent R2 and fluent R1 stage-end profiles.
evidenceDesign: Bind actual R2 language/script separately from R1.
Record both receptive and productive use rather than infer writing from recognition.
nearMisses: R1 success copied across into R2.
Replacing the source frequent subset with a universal 26-letter demand.
protocols.transfer: Use another word/sentence within the declared R2 materials.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: No unqualified alphabet or complete-R2-mastery link is published; material binding is a framework use condition, not a need to choose a national fixed pair now.
